subject: Energy
title: Energy and Human Progress
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Energy and Human Progress.

hook.text: Every leap in civilization was fueled by an energy breakthrough—fire, agriculture, steam, oil, and electricity.

buildup.text: A modern American uses 300 times more energy daily than a prehistoric human—almost entirely from fossil fuels.

discovery.text: GDP and energy use are tightly correlated—wealthy nations consume vastly more energy per capita than poor ones.

twist.text: Some nations are decoupling growth from energy—using efficiency to grow GDP while energy use stays flat.

climax.text: The challenge is providing prosperity without fossil fuels—meeting rising demand with clean energy sources.

punchline.text: More energy, more progress—but the source matters now.

quiz.question: How much more energy does a modern American use than a prehistoric human?
